1: # csv-tools
2: 
3: `csv-tools` is a command line over comma-separated files, written for Node.js with no dependency outside `node:` built-ins. This file is the whole specification: the departments of the program build against it, and `test/` is the committed suite that decides whether they did.
4: 
5: Three subcommands: `stats` reports per-column count, minimum, maximum and mean over numeric columns; `filter` prints the rows whose named column matches an operator and a value; `join` inner-joins two files on a named column.
6: 
7: ## Layout
8: 
9: | Path | Owner |
10: | --- | --- |
11: | `bin/csv-tools.js` | committed at the base revision; nothing changes it |
12: | `test/*.test.js` | committed at the base revision; nothing changes it |
13: | `src/csv.js` | the `stats` department: the shared reader and writer |
14: | `src/stats.js` | the `stats` department |
15: | `src/filter.js` | the `filter` department |
16: | `src/join.js` | the `join` department |
17: 
18: Every department branch is cut from the same base revision, so a department sees no file another department writes. `src/filter.js` and `src/join.js` therefore import nothing at all, and only `bin/csv-tools.js` — which the merged head carries — composes the reader with a subcommand. `src/stats.js` may import `src/csv.js`, because the same department owns both.
19: 
20: Install nothing. A `node_modules` directory in the worktree fails the department's own check.
21: 
22: ## The CSV dialect
23: 
24: An RFC 4180 subset, with a comma delimiter and `"` as the quote character.
25: 
26: - Records are terminated by CRLF, LF or a lone CR. One terminator at the very end of the document closes the last record without starting an empty one, so `a\n` and `a` are both one record while `a\n\n` is two and `\n` is one record holding one empty field. A document with no characters has no records.
27: - A field is quoted only when `"` is its very first character. Inside the quotes a doubled `""` stands for one literal quote, and commas and terminators are data. After the closing quote only a comma, a terminator or the end of the document may follow; anything else is `unexpected character after closing quote: <character>`. A `"` anywhere else in a field is ordinary text.
28: - A quoted field the document never closes is `unterminated quoted field`.
29: - Fields are never trimmed, and an empty field is preserved wherever it appears.
30: - The first record is the header. Its names are used verbatim; a repeated name is `duplicate column: <name>`. A document with no records at all is `input has no header record`.
31: - Every data row carries exactly as many fields as the header; otherwise `row <n>: expected <h> fields, got <g>`, where `n` counts data rows from 1.
32: 
33: Output is written in the same dialect with LF terminators, one after every record including the last. A field is quoted, with every embedded `"` doubled, exactly when it contains a comma, a `"`, a CR or an LF.
34: 
35: ## Module contracts
36: 
37: A table is `{ header: string[], rows: string[][] }`.
38: 
39: - `src/csv.js` exports `parseCsv(text) -> table`, `formatCsv(table) -> string` and `escapeField(value) -> string`.
40: - `src/stats.js` exports `stats(table) -> table`.
41: - `src/filter.js` exports `filter(table, column, operator, value) -> table`.
42: - `src/join.js` exports `join(left, right, column) -> table`.
43: 
44: Every failure is an `Error` whose `code` property is `'usage'` when the command line itself is wrong and `'data'` when the input is. The message is the diagnostic, without a prefix and without a trailing newline.
45: 
46: ## What is a number
47: 
48: One rule, used by `stats` for recognising a numeric column and by `filter` for `<` and `>`: a value is a number when it matches `-?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` from end to end. A leading `+`, a leading zero (`007`), a bare `.5`, `NaN` and `Infinity` are not numbers, so a column of zero-padded identifiers is text.
49: 
50: A printed number is `String(Math.round(value * 1e6) / 1e6)`, so a result is rounded to six decimal places and an integer keeps its plain form.
51: 
52: ## `stats`
53: 
54: `csv-tools stats <file>` prints the header `column,count,min,max,mean` and then one record per numeric column, in header order.
55: 
56: A column is numeric when it has at least one non-empty value and every non-empty value in it is a number. Empty values are skipped rather than counted, so `count` is the number of non-empty values and a column of only empty values is not numeric. A file whose columns are all text prints the header record alone.
57: 
58: ## `filter`
59: 
60: `csv-tools filter <file> <column> <operator> <value>` prints the header record and then every row whose `<column>` cell matches.
61: 
62: The operators are `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>` and `contains`. `=` and `!=` compare the cell and the value as strings. `contains` is a case-sensitive substring test. `<` and `>` compare numerically when the cell and the value are both numbers and otherwise compare the two strings by UTF-16 code unit. An operator outside the five is the usage error `unknown operator: <operator>`; a column outside the header is the data error `unknown column: <column>`. A filter nothing matches prints the header record alone and succeeds.
63: 
64: ## `join`
65: 
66: `csv-tools join <left> <right> <column>` prints the inner join of the two files on `<column>`.
67: 
68: The output header is the left header followed by every right column except the join column. One output row is emitted for each pair of a left row and a right row whose `<column>` cells are equal as strings, left rows in file order outermost and right rows in file order innermost, so a key repeated on both sides yields every pair.
69: 
70: `<column>` missing from either header is the data error `unknown column: <column>`. A right column carried into the output whose name is already in the left header is the data error `duplicate column: <name>`.
71: 
72: ## Exit codes and channels
73: 
74: | Code | Meaning |
75: | --- | --- |
76: | `0` | the subcommand succeeded |
77: | `1` | the command line is wrong: no subcommand, an unknown subcommand, the wrong number of arguments, an unknown operator |
78: | `2` | the input is wrong: a file that cannot be read, a malformed document, an unknown or duplicate column |
79: 
80: A successful run writes the result to stdout and nothing at all to stderr. A failing run writes nothing to stdout and exactly one line to stderr, `csv-tools: <message>`, terminated by LF.
81: 
82: The argument counts are `stats` 1, `filter` 4 and `join` 3. A wrong count is `<subcommand> takes <n> argument(s), got <m>`, and a missing or unknown subcommand is `expected one of stats, filter, join, got <word>` — `nothing` when the command line is empty.

(End of file - total 82 lines)
</content>

3:  * The csv-tools command line: validate the argument list, read the input files,
4:  * dispatch to the subcommand module and write the table it returns.
5:  *
6:  * This file is committed at the base revision and no department changes it. It
7:  * is also the only place the reader and a subcommand meet: a department branch
8:  * carries one module and cannot load another's, so the modules are composed
9:  * here and nowhere else.
10:  */
11: 
12: import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
13: 
14: /** Arguments each subcommand takes after its own name. */
15: const ARITY = { stats: 1, filter: 4, join: 3 };
16: 
17: /** Exit code per error class; anything unclassified is an input failure. */
18: const EXIT = { usage: 1, data: 2 };
19: 
20: /**
21:  * @param {string} message diagnostic, without prefix or terminator
22:  * @returns {Error} a wrong-command-line failure
23:  */
24: function usageError(message) {
25:   const error = new Error(message);
26:   error.code = 'usage';
27:   return error;
28: }
29: 
30: /**
31:  * @param {string} message diagnostic, without prefix or terminator
32:  * @returns {Error} a wrong-input failure
33:  */
34: function dataError(message) {
35:   const error = new Error(message);
36:   error.code = 'data';
37:   return error;
38: }
39: 
40: /**
41:  * @param {string} path file to read
42:  * @returns {string} its UTF-8 text
43:  */
44: function readText(path) {
45:   try {
46:     return readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
47:   } catch {
48:     // Absent, a directory, or unreadable: one diagnostic covers all three.
49:     throw dataError(`cannot read ${path}`);
50:   }
51: }
52: 
53: /**
54:  * Run one command line.
55:  *
56:  * @param {string[]} argv arguments after the program name
57:  * @returns {Promise<string>} the document to write to stdout
58:  */
59: async function run(argv) {
60:   const [command, ...args] = argv;
61:   if (command === undefined || !Object.hasOwn(ARITY, command)) {
62:     throw usageError(`expected one of ${Object.keys(ARITY).join(', ')}, got ${command ?? 'nothing'}`);
63:   }
64:   if (args.length !== ARITY[command]) {
65:     throw usageError(`${command} takes ${ARITY[command]} argument(s), got ${args.length}`);
66:   }
67:   const { parseCsv, formatCsv } = await import('../src/csv.js');
68:   if (command === 'stats') {
69:     const { stats } = await import('../src/stats.js');
70:     return formatCsv(stats(parseCsv(readText(args[0]))));
71:   }
72:   if (command === 'filter') {
73:     const { filter } = await import('../src/filter.js');
74:     return formatCsv(filter(parseCsv(readText(args[0])), args[1], args[2], args[3]));
75:   }
76:   const { join } = await import('../src/join.js');
77:   return formatCsv(join(parseCsv(readText(args[0])), parseCsv(readText(args[1])), args[2]));
78: }
79: 
80: try {
81:   process.stdout.write(await run(process.argv.slice(2)));
82: } catch (error) {
83:   process.stderr.write(`csv-tools: ${error.message}\n`);
84:   process.exitCode = EXIT[error.code] ?? EXIT.data;
85: }

(End of file - total 85 lines)
</content>

Done. `src/join.js` is delivered and committed on the `join` department branch (commit `685e59a`), with `node --test test/join.test.js` passing 7/7 over a clean worktree.

**What I built**

`join(left, right, column)` — the only export, and the module imports nothing, per SPEC.md §Layout (a department branch can't load another department's file; the reader and the subcommand meet only in `bin/csv-tools.js`).

- **Header** — the left header followed by every right column except the join column, in right-header order.
- **Rows** — right rows are bucketed by key preserving file order, then walked once per left row. That gives left-outermost / right-innermost ordering, so a key repeated on both sides yields every pair, while staying linear instead of O(n·m).
- **String equality** — keys are compared as raw cell strings, so `01` and `1` never match.
- **Errors** — both are `Error`s with `code: 'data'` and an unprefixed, unterminated message: `unknown column: <column>` when the column is absent from *either* header, and `duplicate column: <name>` when a carried right column repeats a left one.

**Verification beyond the suite.** I probed corners the tests don't reach: a join column that isn't the first column, empty row sets, and error precedence — a column missing from the right header reports `unknown column` even when a duplicate carried name also exists, which matches the spec's ordering (a column has to exist before carrying is considered). I also confirmed the input tables aren't mutated and output rows aren't aliased to input rows, since rows are built with fresh spreads.

**Constraints respected.** `bin/csv-tools.js` and `test/` are untouched — the commit is a single added file, 76 insertions. Nothing was installed; there is no `node_modules` in the worktree, which the spec notes would fail the department's own check.

One thing worth flagging for whoever merges: the full `npm test` run can't pass on this branch alone, because `test/cli.test.js` and `test/csv.test.js` need `src/csv.js` from the `stats` department. That's expected from the branch layout, and `test/join.test.js` — the stated measure for this department — passes standalone.
